entityDescription:
Composites ATE is a Spanish industrial company specialised in advanced composite manufacturing, industrialisation and high-performance insulation solutions, serving the aerospace, space, railway, defence, industrial and other demanding mobility and engineering sectors.
At its Barcelona facility, ATE develops and industrialises composite manufacturing processes for carbon, glass and natural-fibre components, with particular expertise in prepreg compression moulding, out-of-autoclave processing and accelerated curing technologies. Its capabilities include tooling and production means development, CNC trimming and machining, bonding, assembly, painting and the industrialisation of both prototypes and recurring series. ATE works mainly on a built-to-print basis, supporting customers from process definition and tooling through qualification and serial production.
ATE’s Zaragoza operations complement these capabilities with industrial insulation and technical laminate solutions for electrical, thermal and mechanical applications. Activities include machining of insulating materials and technical laminates, production of customised insulation components, mould and tooling machining, casting and related industrial processes, as well as the manufacture and integration of components for demanding industrial applications.
Together, the two sites provide ATE with a broad multisector industrial capability combining advanced composites, insulation technologies, tooling, machining and production engineering, from low-volume high-performance applications to recurrent industrial manufacturing.

The Romanian Meteorological Service was set up in July 1884, being one of the oldest scientific institutions in Romania. Romania is a founding member of the World Meteorological Organization. The meteorological activity continued unabated under different forms of administrative organization.
The National Meteorological Administration was set up in 1999, as a result of the administrative reorganization of the National Company "National Institute of Meteorology, Hydrology and Water Management" SA.
The legislative regulations of these administrative measures were later adopted by Law no. 139/2000 regarding the meteorological activity and by the Law no. 216/2004 on the establishment of the National Meteorological Administration.

Since 2004, we have been successfully operating in the digital communication sector, exploring new approaches and forms of expression with the aim of providing our clients with a comprehensive service based on coherent and effective creativity. We help our clients transform ideas into coordinated actions and into products with strong creative and commercial value.
We are a team of professionals who combine their distinctive skills and expertise to provide solutions, consultancy services and technical support tailored to the different needs of each client.
Le Fucine communication agency began its operations in Perugia in 2004, where it is still based today. Its 160-square-metre premises are located in a building surrounded by greenery in Strada Tuderte. The agency has a permanent team of six employees and three external collaborators working across a range of areas, including project development and creative services, video production, web development, account management, copywriting, administration and secretarial support.
Le Fucine provides companies and clients with specialised and efficient services designed to support their growth in the fields of marketing and communication. Its contribution covers a broad range of activities, from strategic and marketing analysis to consultancy in communication and public relations.
Since 2022, Le Fucine has been responsible of managing Unipg Shop Official Merchandising. This assignment plays an important role for the University of Perugia, ensuring the careful and consistent development and implementation of products carrying the University’s institutional brand.
Le Fucine oversees detailed production planning and works closely with established suppliers to ensure that all products comply with the high quality standards required.
At the same time, Le Fucine develops highly targeted marketing strategies across a variety of communication and distribution channels, with the aim of increasing the visibility and market penetration of the University of Perugia’s merchandising products.
This strategic approach not only strengthens the University’s institutional identity, but also creates a strong and tangible connection between the University and its community of supporters, fostering deeper and more lasting engagement.
Our services and products:
Video Production and Live Streaming

Communication and Graphic Design

Web and Multimedia

Tuco Marine Group is a Danish shipyard based in Faaborg, Denmark, designing and manufacturing high-performance professional workboats under the ProZero brand for commercial, offshore, defence and workboat operators. Vessels are built in composite (fibreglass/carbon-fibre) construction rather than aluminium or steel, giving lower weight, higher speed, lower fuel consumption and a longer operational lifetime, with easier repair after damage. Tuco's vessels are SOLAS and DNV certified.
Tuco's portfolio also includes uncrewed surface vessel (USV) platforms, such as the ProZero 8m USV, used for surveillance and data-acquisition missions and delivered to defence and commercial operators. Truco y Trufa SL (T&T) is a Spanish SME based in Madrid. Its technology unit, t&tech, applies statistical modelling and machine learning to problems where labelled data is scarce, signals are weak, and decisions must be made under real constraints.

Current work spans unsupervised anomaly detection in time-series telemetry, including a detector for spacecraft housekeeping data validated against real in-orbit events; synthetic population modelling built on national statistical microdata for simulating behaviour at population scale; geospatial and remote-sensing analysis; and automated intelligence systems that extract structure from heterogeneous public sources.

A recurring focus is making these methods deployable: deterministic, reproducible, auditable, and small enough to run within tight memory and compute budgets rather than only in a research notebook.

Its instrument, METRON, provides independent, external, read-only measurement of system behaviour from existing archives, telemetry and OpenTelemetry flows: autonomy rate, behavioural baseline and drift over time, detection and reaction latency under disruption, and unreported data gaps. Measurements are sealed into tamper-evident evidence, verifiable by third parties, suitable for audit and qualification.
Capabilities demonstrated on 17 years of publicly available ESA mission data, 3.5 million executions. Domains: Resilient PNT, ground segment and mission operations, independent verification and validation, and incident lessons-learned registries.

Our core business covers the heavy overhaul of electrical, electronic, pneumatic and mechanical subassemblies removed from trains, tramways and metro vehicles: circuit breakers, braking equipment, HVAC units, on-board electronics and associated components. Our capabilities include failure analysis and diagnostics, component-level repair, obsolescence management and re-engineering of discontinued parts, functional testing on dedicated test benches, and full lifecycle documentation.
MASTERIS works for national and regional rail operators, urban transport authorities and rolling stock manufacturers across Europe, delivering long-term maintenance contracts as well as one-off overhaul and retrofit programmes.

entityDescription:
Zenith Pulse GmbH — Company Description (EN)
Zenith Pulse GmbH is a German company based in Baden-Württemberg developing a software platform that calculates a company's actual carbon footprint directly from its suppliers' invoices, processed through a proprietary algorithm, and generates a Scope 1/2/3 emissions report with concrete reduction recommendations. Built on this core engine, Zenith Pulse is developing additional verticals that integrate Copernicus (Sentinel) and NASA Earth observation data to enrich the analysis with land-use monitoring, coastal-zone assessment, pollution and urban heat-island detection, physical climate risk, and resource-use intelligence.
The product addresses a regulatory-driven need: the EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) requires companies to report Scope 1/2/3 emissions, while smaller suppliers face indirect pressure to provide the same data to larger corporate customers. Target customers include both private companies (B2B) and German municipalities, served through modular subscription packages.
A working prototype of the core Scope 1/2/3 calculation engine is operational, using recognized, publicly documented emission-factor sources. The satellite-data verticals are in development and have not yet been validated with a paying customer.
The founding team combines engineering and entrepreneurial experience with software architecture and IoT research expertise, supported by a specialist in GIS and remote sensing for satellite data integration.

entityDescription:
Sagittal Optics S.L. is a specialized engineering company delivering high-performance optical and opto-mechanical solutions for space and ground-based instrumentation, broadband imaging, laser systems, and sensing applications. The company supports the full development cycle: optical architecture trade-offs, detailed optical design and simulation, tolerance and sensitivity analysis, stray light and ghost mitigation (non-sequential analysis), and opto-mechanical design validated through structural, thermal, and optical simulations (STOP).
Sagittal Optics is based in the Canary Islands (Spain) and is built around a team with extensive international experience in space and astronomy instrumentation, including long-term work on major observatories and complex opto-mechanical/cryogenic systems, as well as industrial R&D and prototyping environments. This background enables practical, verification-driven designs that consider manufacturing, alignment, and test constraints from the earliest phases.
Sagittal Optics also provides AIV-oriented engineering, including alignment strategies, test setup definition, and performance verification planning, helping customers reduce technical risk and shorten development timelines. The company maintains prototyping and integration capability, including laboratory setups for optical/mechanical integration and testing, as well as in-house tooling and rapid iteration resources.
Sagittal Optics’ design philosophy focuses on achieving broadband chromatic correction with a minimized number of optical elements, improving transmission, reducing complexity, and enabling more robust, cost-effective systems.

entityDescription: Paraxiom Technologies Inc. is a Canadian SME (Montréal, incorporated 2023) specializing in post-quantum secure communications software. Its core product, PQTG (Post-Quantum Transport Gateway), secures the ETSI GS QKD 014 key-delivery layer of quantum key distribution networks with post-quantum cryptography (ML-KEM-768, Falcon-512, SLH-DSA; pure-Rust implementation), closing the residual classical-TLS exposure in front of quantum-distributed keys. PQTG completed a 9/9 ETSI-014 conformance validation against a production evolutionQ Basejump KMS on Canada's KirQ national quantum testbed and operated live with Toshiba QKD hardware supplying keys. Supporting capabilities include an operating post-quantum distributed ledger for attestation and notarization, a post-quantum SSH implementation, and a formal-verification discipline in Lean aligned with certification-oriented assurance. Areas of interest for ESA activities: ground-segment security for optical and QKD satellite communications, post-quantum key management and identity for governmental 5G/6G non-terrestrial networks, and crypto-agile key-combination architectures (ETSI TS 103 744 / NIST SP 800-227 direction). The company's cryptographic core is under contract for independent technical assessment (BeatQuantum Ltd., UK).

- Bespoke Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) and test solutions

We believe there is a $25Bn underserved and currently disenfranchised, market opportunity for this new vehicle-class, alongside its positive social and environmental benefits.

Company description: The Common Wadden Sea Secretariat (CWSS) supports, facilitates and coordinates the Trilateral Wadden Sea Cooperation (TWSC). Located in Wilhelmshaven, the Secretariat was founded in 1987 by the Wadden Sea states Denmark, Germany, and the Netherlands.
The Secretariat
- coordinates, promotes and supports activities of the Cooperation;
- is responsible for the preparation and production of documents for ministerial conferences, meetings of the Wadden Sea Board (WSB) and trilateral work groups;
- collects and evaluates information on monitoring, protection and the ecological condition of the entire Wadden Sea;
- is the central contact for the UNESCO Wadden Sea World Heritage;
- produces and publishes reports by the Cooperation;
- involves the public in the protection of the entire Wadden Sea area through communications, awareness building and environmental education.
Since the inscription of the Wadden Sea on the UNESCO World Heritage List, the Secretariat moreover deals with the implementation of the obligations derived from the UNESCO World Heritage Convention.
The legal status and the functions of and regulations governing CWSS are stipulated in the Administrative Agreement concluded between the Danish, Dutch and German Ministries responsible for the Wadden Sea. Each Ministry finances a third of its budget. The working language of the Trilateral Cooperation and the CWSS is English.

INGECID S.L. is an engineering firm founded in 2009, with its headquarters in Santander and offices in Madrid and Bilbao, as well as international subsidiaries in Germany, Norway, South Africa, and the United States. Its corporate purpose is to conduct research and innovation in the fields of construction technology, software engineering, renewable energy, and nuclear energy, collaborating with research groups on the development of R&D projects. Innovation is a central element of its business strategy, which has resulted throughout its history in the generation of a large number of national and international patents and in the delivery of high-value-added technological solutions to the market.
INGECID has a multidisciplinary technical team of approximately 100 people (40% women), organized into areas of activity that include the management and development of R&D&I projects, software development, generative design, structural engineering, technical consulting, and radiological engineering, among others. As a certified entity, it has an R&D&I management unit composed of a specialized research team.
The company has established an Integrated Management System certified to the ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, UNE-EN ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and UNE-EN ISO 56001:2024, whose scope encompasses training, research, development, and innovation in projects and software in the fields of civil engineering, renewable energy, and nuclear energy. The company’s own resources allocated to R&D include design, programming, and data analysis tools; BIM software; and the VIRCORE platform (developed by INGECID) which is used as a collaborative project management environment.

entityName: University of Passau - Chair of Computer Networks and Computer Communications
entityDescription:
The Chair of Computer Networks And Computer Communications at the University of Passau has its main areas of research in satellite communication, network analysis and virtualization, self-organizing systems, IT security, safety and energy efficiency.
In regard to satellites, the team's research assesses the potential of satellite technologies for the energy system, particularly of satellite communications and Earth observation. In Earth observation, the team's interest is in studying how satellites can enhance situational awareness by acting as an additional source of information and by processing data at the edge. In satellite communications, the research focuses on how satellites can contribute to the resilience of the power grid, for example by providing a redundant communication path.
The Chair of Computer Networks And Computer Communications has experience in satellite communications from both completed and ongoing projects: In EnerSat, a feasibility study, satellite networks were studied for reliable monitoring of critical infrastructure. In STARS, the potential of satellite communication to combat blackouts was assessed. In KRISNet a flat sat is being developed to demonstrate multi-channel communication via both terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks to enhance the resilience of the power grid.
